meta.title: World of VerseCraft
meta.blurb: Welcome to the world of VerseCraft! Enjoy the story and immerse yourself in the deep storytelling, meaningful choices and RPG elements to create worlds of enjoyment.

S01.text:
The road was supposed to be simple.
One town to the next. A roof, maybe a fire, then gone again before morning. 
That was the deal you made with yourself when you left the last place behind.
The storm came faster than expected.

Rain lashes sideways, soaking through your clothes until every step feels heavier than the last. 
The road ahead dissolves into mud and broken stone, the path barely visible through sheets of water and wind.
Then the lightning hits.
For a split second, the tower reveals itself—vast, looming, impossible to miss once seen. 
Its doors hang shattered, blasted outward as if something inside fled in desperation.

You slow your pace.
Shelter is shelter.
But you’ve learned the hard way that the places that promise safety often charge more than they give.
The wind screams louder. The cold bites deeper.

Staying out here is no longer an option.


ATTEMPT TO LEAVE -- You decide there must be a better option than trying to take refuge in this hastily abandoned tower.

ENTER THE TOWER -- Despite your trepidation about the tower, you enter seeking shelter.

FIND ANOTHER ENTRANCE -- Attempt to find another way in to the tower, avoiding the main entrance entirely.

S02.text:
You turn away from the tower.

The rain greets you like a wall.

Wind howls across the road, louder than before, bending the world sideways. 
Water surges down the path you arrived on, swallowing the ruts and stones beneath it. 
Each step back feels heavier, slower—like the ground itself is resisting you.

You make it only a short distance before the road gives way.

Mud collapses underfoot. The path you followed here is gone, torn open by the storm 
and dragged downhill into the dark. What remains is impassable—a slick, churning slope 
that leads nowhere.

You look back.

The tower stands unchanged.

Its doors hang open, blasted outward, as if something inside once fled in desperation. 
Light flickers faintly within—not inviting, not welcoming—but present.

The storm presses closer behind you.

Whatever choice brought you here, the world has decided something else.

There is only one way forward now.

S03.text:
You cross the threshold.
The change is immediate.
The storm does not fade—it cuts off. Rain still lashes the shattered doors behind you, 
but the sound arrives late and distant, muffled by layers of stone that should not exist.
The tower does not welcome you.
It accepts you.
Inside, the air is dry and stale, carrying the faint scent of dust and old ash. 
Pale seams of light glow between the stones beneath your feet, dim but deliberate, 
like embers buried under the floor.
The doors behind you hang twisted and broken, blasted outward with violent force. 
Whatever came through them did not hesitate.

Ahead, the interior opens into a vast chamber. Stairways spiral upward along the walls, 
vanishing into shadow. Corridors slope downward into darker depths. Side halls branch away, 
their purposes unclear.
This place is old.
Not abandoned.
Waiting.
For a brief moment, you have the distinct impression that something is aware of you.

Watching.

Measuring.

The feeling slips away before it can take shape.
The storm surges once more against the doors—then falls silent again.
Whatever happens next will not happen on the road.
It will happen here.

DEEPER INTO TOWER -- Move deeper into the tower cautiously.

SEARCH SIDE CHAMBER -- Check around to see if there may be something of use nearby.

GO UP STAIRS -- Head towards te stairwell. Another decision looms.

S04.text:
You stay in the rain longer than you should.
Circling the tower’s base, you search for anything that might pass for a safer way inside. 
The stone walls are slick and uneven, the mortar crumbling beneath years of neglect. 
Water runs in thin streams down the surface, blurring old carvings and half-erased symbols.
You look up.
The second story is too high. The windows are narrow, their edges fractured and unstable. 
No ledges you’d trust. No clear handholds. Whatever force broke the doors below did not 
bother with subtlety above.
The wind cuts harder now, driving the rain into your face. Cold settles into your bones.
There’s no way in except the obvious one.

GIVE UP AND RETURN -- Go back to the front entrance of the tower.

KEEP SEACRHING -- See if maybe you can climb up the stony tower sides, but they are slippery.

S05.text:
You move around the back of the tower, keeping low and quiet.
Here, the stone shows its age—cracks in the masonry, repairs long abandoned, 
edges softened by time and weather. Your eyes trace a narrow route upward toward a first-story window, 
half-shattered and dark beyond.
You start climbing.
Rain slicks the stone beneath your fingers, but the footholds hold—until they don’t. 
With a sharp crack, part of the window frame crumbles away. You lunge forward, 
barely catching yourself as debris falls into the darkness below.
You’re stuck.
The ground is too far down to drop safely. The way back is gone. Above you, the tower rises higher, 
unforgiving and wet.

ATTEMPT TO CLIMB HIGHER -- Press your luck and try to reach the next story up.

SEARCH CHAMBER -- Take a moment to look around and find something useful.

TRY TO GET DOWN -- Attempt to drop down and get back to the front entrance.

S06.text:
You look up.
The tower stretches above you, its stone slick with rain and age. 
The window you aimed for is gone now, crumbled away into darkness below. 
Your arms tremble as you cling to what remains, fingers numb, muscles burning.

Going down isn’t an option anymore.
You shift your weight carefully, testing the stone above you. Some holds feel solid. 
Others flake away at the slightest pressure. Water runs down the wall, blurring edges 
and making every movement uncertain.
For a moment, doubt creeps in.
Then you push it aside.

You’ve climbed worse. Broken into tighter places. Bet your life on thinner margins.
You pull yourself upward.
The stone gives way without warning.

TRY TO CATCH YOURSELF -- Attempt to grab something solid and not fall.

BRACE FOR IMPACT --  Cover and tuck and roll.

S07.text:
You emerge into darkness and stone.
The opening you pulled yourself through is narrow and broken, 
its edges worn smooth by years of weather and neglect. Behind you, rain still lashes the tower’s outer wall, 
but the sound fades quickly, swallowed by the thickness of the stone. 
Whatever storm rages outside does not fully exist in here.
The air is different.

Dry. Still. Heavy in a way that settles against your senses rather than your lungs. 
Old magic lingers here—not active, not fading, simply present. 
Your own power doesn’t rest easily. It hums beneath your skin, unsettled, 
as if something nearby is paying closer attention than it should.
You pause to steady yourself.
The climb—or the spell—has taken more from you than you expected. 
Your muscles ache. Your breath comes shallow and slow. 
Whatever force governs this tower does not reward cleverness. 
It demands payment before allowing progress.
Faint light traces the seams between the stones beneath your feet. 
It doesn’t brighten the chamber, only outlines it enough for you to understand its shape. 
The space is small. Enclosed. From it, a corridor curves away along the tower’s interior, 
following its circular spine.

No windows.

No obvious exits beyond the passage ahead.

Then, a voice.
Not loud. Not whispered. Simply there.
“You came in through the wrong place.”
The words settle into your thoughts as if they belong there. The tone isn’t hostile—just tired. 
Flat. As though this is an observation it has made too many times to care anymore.

A brief pause follows.
“Most of them don’t try that.”

The air tightens, almost imperceptibly. Not a threat. More like attention being focused. 
You get the sense that something has adjusted—not rushed, not alarmed, but deliberate.
The light beneath your feet pulses once, then settles again. Somewhere deeper in the tower, stone shifts against stone. Slow. Controlled.
Whatever rules this place knows where you are now.
The corridor ahead opens toward a wider space, its curve easing as the ceiling rises out of sight. The pressure in the air deepens as you look on—not heavier, just more complete. Whatever lies further inside is no longer hidden.
It is waiting.

S08.text:
You don’t catch yourself in time.
Your grip slips completely, and the tower vanishes from reach as gravity takes hold. 

The fall is short—but violent. You hit the ground hard, breath exploding from your lungs 
as pain rips through your side and leg.
Rain pounds down on you as you lie there, stunned and gasping.
Nothing feels broken.

But nothing feels right either.

Every movement sends sharp pain through your body, and when you try to stand, 
your leg buckles beneath you. You manage to stagger upright, leaning heavily on the wall for support.
Climbing again is impossible.
Whatever you hoped to gain by avoiding the main entrance, it isn’t worth this.
You limp toward the shattered doors, each step slower than the last.
